topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: The Hook: From Average to Instantaneous
sections.content: Begin with a visual animation of a cheetah running. Define the 'Average Velocity' over a long interval (total distance/total time). Transition to the problem: How fast is the cheetah moving at the exact moment it pounces? Introduce the concept of shrinking the time interval towards zero.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed = 20 m/s. But what about the exact speed at t=2 seconds?

sections.title: Visualizing the Secant Line
sections.content: Graph a curve f(x). Show two points, A and B, connected by a secant line. Explain that the slope of this line represents the average rate of change. As B slides along the curve toward A, the secant line transforms into a tangent line.
sections.example: An animation showing a blue secant line gradually rotating into a red tangent line as point B approaches point A.

sections.title: The Mathematical Definition
sections.content: Introduce the formal limit definition of the derivative: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Break down the components: (f(x+h)-f(x)) as the 'rise' and (h) as the 'run'. Explain that as h becomes infinitely small, the average rate becomes the instantaneous rate.
sections.example: Using the function f(x) = x² to demonstrate the algebraic limit process resulting in f'(x) = 2x.

sections.title: Practical Application: Motion Tracking
sections.content: Connect the derivative back to the cheetah. If the position of the cheetah is given by s(t), the derivative s'(t) represents the instantaneous velocity. This reinforces the 'Derivative = Rate of Change' intuition.
sections.example: A digital speedometer on a screen updating in real-time as a virtual character accelerates, showing that the derivative is the 'rate' at any specific tick of the clock.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Synthesize the lesson: The derivative is the mathematical tool for analyzing 'instantaneous' behavior. It turns global information (the whole curve) into local information (the slope at a single point).
sections.example: A quick visual overlay showing the relationship: Function (Position) → Derivative (Velocity) → Instantaneous Change.
